title: Multi-Task Learning for Routing Problem with Cross-Problem Zero-Shot Generalization

problem.claim: Cross-problem generalization in neural combinatorial optimization for vehicle routing problems.

gap.claim: Existing neural combinatorial optimization methods often build a different model for each routing problem, hindering applications involving many vehicle-routing variants.

contributions.claim: Formulates vehicle-routing problems as combinations of shared underlying attributes and solves them simultaneously with a single model through attribute composition.
Enables zero-shot solution of vehicle-routing problems with unseen attribute combinations.

stated_novelty.claim: The work presents a first attempt to address cross-problem generalization in neural combinatorial optimization.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The model was trained on five vehicle-routing variants and tested on eleven variants.
The authors report superior performance across the eleven variants, reducing the average gap to around 5% from over 20%.
The authors report notable performance improvements on benchmark datasets and real-world logistics scenarios.

narrative_sequence.summary: Vehicle-routing problems are important in real-world applications, and neural combinatorial optimization has attracted increasing research attention.
Existing methods commonly require a separate model for each routing problem, limiting cross-problem applicability.
The work composes shared routing attributes in one model to solve multiple variants and generalize to unseen combinations.
Experiments train on five variants and test on eleven, with reported improvements in average gap and performance across benchmark and real-world settings.

source_observation.claim: A single model composes shared underlying attributes to address multiple problem variants.

interpretation.claim: Representing related task variants through shared attributes may support transfer to combinations not observed during training.

application.claim: When related tasks share structural attributes, consider multi-task or compositional modeling to reduce the need for separate models.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach generalizes beyond the reported vehicle-routing variants or settings.

unknowns: The specific shared attributes and model architecture are not described.
Dataset details, baselines, evaluation metrics, and experimental conditions are not provided.
